items.title: Ousted Nvidia boss may have bigger problems than getting his job back

Share A A A A petition calling for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief executive has already surpassed 187,000 signatures. Donald Trump “wouldn’t mind” if he regained the role.

Huang himself is said to be pondering whether he should reconsider his decision to resign in response to the revelations of his affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and, reportedly, Nvidia executives -- although the AI giant’s board seems committed to its search for his replacement , and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is urging for a complete outsider to replace him.

Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before US House politicians on his relationship with Alice Huang. Getty The petition’s website – “Stand with Jensen” – is being overwhelmed by a torrent of signatures of support from senior Nvidia employees, current and former staff, Silicon Valley leaders and Nvidia shareholders.
Elon Musk and Trump are encouraging them from the sidelines, with Musk saying Nvidia would lose critical deals without Huang and that it would be “an honour” to hire him.

The AI sector is fearful that without Huang, whose deals have a handshake quality to them, Nvidia might not be able to maintain its role in supplying chips and vendor financing - and providing guarantees to financiers - to a large part of the AI ecosystem.
“I would not mind; I wouldn’t mind that,” he said. “I think he learned a big lesson – I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another.”
The US president also questioned whether Alice Huang (no relation), the woman at the centre of the controversy, was actually a Chinese spy.

“I don’t know that she was a spy. Usually what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy. I don’t know that she was a spy at all.”

US intelligence agencies, according to the New York Times , does suspect Alice Huang of being a spy. Secretary of State Marco Rubio wrote to Trump warning him of those suspicions, although Trump says he hadn’t heard that.

What doesn’t appear to have occurred to Trump or the thousands of people signing the petition to bring Jensen back, is that the question of whether Alice Huang was or wasn’t a spy isn’t the central issue for either the Nvidia board or the US government.

For the board, there’s the more conventional issue of a CEO having an affair with, it’s alleged, the senior executive of a major customer – Megaspeed, where Alice Huang was the CEO at the time of the relationship, acquired many billions of dollars worth of Nvidia’s most advanced chips – and reportedly at least one company subordinate without informing directors. That alone would provide a reason for dumping him.
For the government, the far more critical question is whether MegaSpeed was able, with Nvidia’s help, to circumvent export controls designed to prevent Chinese access to its most advanced chips.
In a sense, it has already answered the question after the horse has bolted by slamming that particular stable door shut.

Donald Trump keeps backing Jensen Huang, and questions whether his paramour was indeed a Chinese spy. AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin On Monday, the Trump administration announced that it would introduce a new rule that would require overseas data centres to obtain a government licence before supplying any significant amount of computing power to companies with headquarters in a group of countries including China and Russia, with data centres required to determine whether customers are linked to those countries.
The US will also demand a licence for exports of advanced chips to companies headquartered in Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.

Megaspeed was based in Singapore. It imported vast quantities of Nvidia chips – far too large a volume for Singapore’s use – with suspicions that they were either smuggled into China or deployed in data centres in South-East Asian countries to train Chinese artificial intelligence models.
One of the last things the Biden administration did, in January last year, was to promulgate a rule establishing a tiered global system to regulate exports of advanced chips.

Tier one was America’s close allies, including Australia, where there was unrestricted access. Tier two covered most other countries – including Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia -where licensing requirements, caps on computing power and security frameworks were imposed. Tier three were countries under US embargoes like China, Russia and Iran.

One of the first things Trump did when he took office last year – after lobbying by Silicon Valley companies, including Nvidia – was to rescind that rule on the basis that it placed too much of an administration burden on US companies and allies.

Without those rules for dealing with exports of advanced chips the US, which has adopted a laissez-faire approach to AI, has been reliant on its “entity list” – a list of organisations and individuals deemed to pose a risk to US interests – to manage exports of sensitive technologies. Companies need a special licence to deal with those entities on the list.

The fallout from Huang’s affairs has put a spotlight on US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under pressure for his rejections of calls from other government departments, well before the scandal surfaced publicly, to place Megaspeed on the entity list, which would have prevented Nvidia from dealing with it.

Despite urgings from Treasury and other departments, Lutnick refused to put Megaspeed on the list, ostensibly because it would, according to Trump in defence of one of his more committed loyalists, risk a “blow-up” with China.

That suggests at least some in the Trump administration were aware, or at least suspected, that Megaspeed might be providing a backdoor entry for Nvidia chips into China – although, given that it was Trump providing the excuse, he may have made it up after the fact to try to help one of his most loyal cabinet members.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is asking the questions that are key to the Nvidia scandal. Bloomberg It is US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent , who has put the controversy and the issue of Huang’s fate into the right perspective.

He argues that Nvidia has to find a new external CEO, that the company needs a “dramatic shake-up” and that there needs to be an investigation into whether the company complied with US export restrictions. (Only Nvidia’s second-best H200 chips are supposed to be accessible to China).

It is important that there be an examination of whether Nvidia “had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions” and whether its senior executives knew that the rules were being bent, he said.
“Was it a low-level fail? Was it in the middle, or was it up in the C-suite?,” Bessent asked.

“Who knew?,” he went on. “These shell companies [used to acquire Nvidia chips that were then on-sold to data centres in South-East Asia or smuggled into China] were obvious, they were being investigated, and did Nvidia use them as a workaround to sell chips to China?”
“Were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?”

It is improbable that no one at Nvidia knew or suspected that the billions of dollars of sales to Megaspeed – a company that Alice Huang helped established as recently as 2023, with the apparent financial backing of Chinese tech giant Alibaba – were destined, directly or indirectly, for China.
Jensen Huang, given his relationship with Alice Huang, should certainly have known if there was anything questionable about Megaspeed’s dealings in his chips.

Who knew what and when will be tested by the Nvidia board’s internal inquiries, the administration’s separate investigation and in a Congressional hearing, before which both Jensen Huang and Lutnick have already been called.
As Bessent alluded to, the most important issue is not really whether Alice Huang was a spy – US intelligence agencies can sort that out.

The key question is if, and how, very large volumes of Nvidia’s most advanced chips – chips regarded as central to America’s AI lead over China – might have dodged US restrictions, and who might have facilitated the flow of those chips.

If Huang was at the centre of a scheme to sell Nvidia chips to China, or he suspected or was aware that China was the end-destination of Megaspeed’s chip purchase, he will have a lot more to worry about than whether he gets his old job back.

items.title: Labor in deep denial over falling real wages
paras: In a recent interview on News 24, Employment Minister Amanda Rishworth tried to defend real wage growth since the Albanese government came to power.
“There is now a three in front of wages growth”, Rishworth said, attempting to place the focus on the rate of nominal wage growth that was in the 2% range under the Coalition.

Since coming to power, the Albanese government has placed a heavy emphasis on increasing wage growth, but unfortunately for Australians and the government’s political fortunes, inflation has outstripped wages.

Share A A A Locksley Resources has kicked off a 5500-metre diamond drilling campaign at its Iron Duke copper-gold project in central New South Wales, the first step in what is likely to become a significant district-scale exploration push.

The program is the company’s first drilling at the project and aims to test extensions to known high-grade, near-surface lodes that remain open along strike and at depth. Iron Duke currently hosts a 1.1 million tonne inferred resource grading 1.11 per cent copper and 0.61 grams per tonne (g/t) gold.

Locksley Resources’ Iron Duke project sits within the Greater Tottenham copper-gold district (pictured) in the prolific Cobar-Girilambone district of central New South Wales. Previous drilling has already outlined high-grade copper-gold lodes over a 700-metre strike length from near surface. Other historical hits include a solid 13-metre intersection grading 1.56 per cent copper and a significant 4.48g/t gold from just 37m downhole.

Other notable past results include 24m assaying 1.53 per cent copper and 1.55g/t gold from 49m, while two further holes delivered 31m at 1.13 per cent copper and 0.96g/t gold from 34m and 24m going 1.07 per cent copper from just 32m.

Importantly, the mineralisation has so far only been defined to around 140m below surface and remains open. The lodes are described as steeply dipping, ranging from two metres to 20m in true thickness.

Locksley’s current program, which comprises up to 28 diamond holes, will test strike and down-dip extensions of the known mineralisation, with roughly half of the historical holes drilled to less than 100m. The company says the number of holes drilled will depend on results as the program progresses. A key focus of the campaign will be a 100m to 150m-long gap at the southern end of the system, which has seen very little drilling despite sitting directly along strike from the high-grade lodes.

Locksley will also conduct infill drilling within the high-grade core to confirm the continuity and geometry of the mineralised shoots. The new diamond core is expected to deliver valuable structural, bulk density and metallurgical data missing from previous reverse-circulation drilling, providing crucial information for future resource estimates and technical studies.

Locksley Resources technical director Ian Stockton said: “The southern gap sits directly along strike from the high-grade lodes and has seen very little drilling. The oriented core should also show us what controls the high-grade shoots, which is a key to growing Iron Duke and targeting future holes.”

The drilling at Iron Duke is just the opening salvo in a much bigger exploration plan for Locksley. The company has a pipeline of targets that could keep the rig seriously busy, with up to 26,000m of drilling across its Greater Tottenham project. That includes a planned 10,000-metre campaign at Mt Royal–Orange Plains to test sparsely drilled ground and chase extensions to known high-grade mineralisation, while Carolina is also in the queue for future drilling.

The company’s Iron Duke project forms part of its broader 1000-square-kilometre Greater Tottenham land package and sits on ground under an option-to-purchase agreement with Sky Metals. The work at Iron Duke comes just days after Locksley unveiled a significant resource upgrade for Greater Tottenham, which now stands at a hefty 10 million tonnes grading 1.1 per cent copper and 0.32g/t gold for 110,000 tonnes of contained copper and 100,000 ounces of gold.
The project sits within the well-endowed Cobar Basin and Lachlan Orogen and is home to major operations such as Tritton, CSA and the giant Cadia Valley.

The NSW State Government has also thrown its weight behind the region’s copper credentials, naming the red metal among five priority commodities in its Critical Minerals Strategy as global electrification and the energy transition fuel surging demand. The government has backed up its ambitions with cold, hard cash, directing co-investment towards exploration, with 21 of 29 projects backed under its latest funding round focused on copper.
With a healthy $13.4 million in the bank at the end of September, the company also appears to be well-funded to pursue its extensive exploration plans.

With drills now turning at Iron Duke for the first time under Locksley’s management, the company is taking its first real shot at growing that resource. If it can extend the known high-grade mineralisation into the southern gap or deeper into the system, things could get interesting very quickly.

items.title: Diaphragm pacer offers paralysed man hope of freedom from ventilator
paras: Carl Mason lives with his daughter Holly since leaving hospital. ( Supplied: Holly Mason )
A rarely performed medical procedure could give Carl Mason the chance to breathe without a ventilator.
Mr Mason says he hopes to return to Tasmania to continue running his business.
A Tasmanian business owner who was left paralysed after a mountain biking accident last year will undergo a rare medical procedure that could allow him to breathe without a ventilator.
Carl Mason was riding with his friends in Hobart when he experienced an accident in August last year, fracturing all the vertebrae in his neck.
Mr Mason, the co-founder of Smitten Merino, told 936 ABC Hobart he had no memory of the incident that would completely change his life.
The spinal injury has left him a tetraplegic or quadriplegic, meaning he has lost sensation in, and function of, his limbs, torso and breathing muscles.
Carl Mason was left with a severe spinal cord injury. ( Supplied: Holly Mason )
He needs to use a ventilator to help him breathe; however, his phrenic nerve, a vital nerve needed for breathing, remains intact.
It means he is able to undergo a minimally invasive procedure called direct diaphragm pacing stimulation to install a diaphragm pacing device, which could allow him to breathe without a ventilator.
It will be performed at the end of the month by one of the only surgeons in the country trained to do the procedure, Mehrdad Nikfarjam.
Dr Nikfarjam said it was a "truly life-changing" procedure that could dramatically improve a patient's quality of life.
US actor Christopher Reeve was one of the first patients with a spinal injury to undergo the then-experimental procedure in 2003.
The procedure has only been performed about a dozen times in Australia since it was first introduced in the early 2010s, Dr Nikfarjam said.
Mr Mason was flown to Melbourne's Austin Hospital soon after the accident last year, where he stayed until July this year.
Carl Mason lives with his daughter Holly in Melbourne. ( Supplied: Holly Mason )
His daughter, Holly Mason, said the knowledge that her father could regain a sense of agency and quality of life had provided hope.
"It's going to give dad and I some freedom; he'll be able to smell again, he'll even be able to breathe; it's a way of calming down anxiety," Ms Mason said.
Mr Mason said despite needing full-time carers and a significant amount of medical equipment, leaving hospital had given him freedom and, for the first time since the accident, access to nature.
"I'm so grateful to her for helping me get out, even if I feel a bit down, to get me out [of] the house," he said.
"She shows me simple things, like a bird in a tree, or a leaf, whatever it is."
He has fought through two bouts of pneumonia and has been intermittently re-hospitalised.
But with surgery scheduled in for the end of this month, his daughter said they could begin to look toward the future again.
"Every single week, every single day, we didn't know if he was going to survive today," Ms Mason said.
Mr Mason remains determined to get back to Tasmania to continue the family business, which is almost two decades old.
Nicola Mason (right) has continued to run the family business. ( Supplied: Holly Mason )
"I'm just hoping to get back to as close as my old life as I can, which sounds a little hilarious," Mr Mason said.
"But if I could just get back, and alongside my beautiful wife Nicola, we could continue to build Smitten; that's my big dream."

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: Robo-soldier startup backed by Eric Trump misses payroll, may collapse
paras: Military vaporware watch Robo-soldier startup backed by Eric Trump misses payroll, may collapse Robotics startup misses payroll a year after CEO used funds for luxury home.

47 ... ... ... A demo video shows a Foundation Future Industries humanoid robot, the Phantom MK-1, taking a mortar shell from a person before lowering it into the mortar weapon muzzle. Credit: Foundation Future Industries A demo video shows a Foundation Future Industries humanoid robot, the Phantom MK-1, taking a mortar shell from a person before lowering it into the mortar weapon muzzle. Credit: Foundation Future Industries Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav A humanoid robotics company backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall. The Silicon Valley startup, Foundation Future Industries, claims it is developing and testing robots for military roles on battlefields from Ukraine to Gaza.

Foundation failed to pay employees for the payroll period ending on October 30, anonymous sources told CNBC . The startup’s staff is especially angry because Foundation’s co-founder and CEO, Sankaet Pathak , supposedly borrowed $4.6 million in company funds to buy a luxury home overlooking San Francisco Bay about a year ago.

This comes as Pathak and Foundation’s leadership are still looking to raise funding to support a $3 billion valuation, based on their promise to develop a humanoid robot ready for combat duty and capable of wielding various weapons.

The company has demonstrated a humanoid robot named the Phantom MK-1 and is touting an upcoming robot called the Phantom MK-2. Foundation has touted its humanoid robots for roles in warehouses and other workplaces—but has courted media coverage by claiming it is developing humanoid robots for battlefield use.
Now CNBC’s reporting based on “people with direct knowledge of the matter” indicates that insiders worry the startup could soon collapse without additional funding.

Eric Trump holds an equity stake in Foundation and was announced as its chief strategy advisor in March 2026, according to the Financial Times . Investment funds linked to both Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. are involved with multiple military technology companies that have received Pentagon loans and contracts worth more than $3.2 billion as of July 2026, according to The Washington Post .

After Trump claimed that Foundation had “just secured a $24 million contract with the Pentagon” during the Fox Business interview in April, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) responded by questioning whether the Pentagon is “just a cash machine from Trump’s kids now” in a social media post . “This looks like corruption in plain sight,” Warren wrote.

But publicly available evidence does not back up Trump’s claim about Foundation directly receiving US government funding. Federal spending records show that Foundation holds no publicly listed contracts, according to The San Francisco Standard .
Instead, the company Boardwalk Robotics received four contracts worth $3.22 million prior to being acquired by Foundation in late 2024.

Meanwhile, the Institute for Human & Machine Cognition—a Florida-based nonprofit research institute and research partner to Boardwalk Robotics—secured a $24.8 million Navy contract in 2025, The San Francisco Standard reported.

This was not the first time that Foundation’s leadership and investors have made unsupported statements. In 2024, General Motors pushed back on Foundation’s claims that it was about to get an investment from the Detroit automaker, according to CNBC .

On November 11, 2026, Mike LeBlanc, co-founder and president of Foundation Future Industries, told the Financial Times that the company was in talks with the Israeli military to provide humanoid robots for patrol and combat duties in Hamas tunnels beneath Gaza. He also described taking the company’s Phantom MK1 humanoid robot along to tour some of the tunnels.
However, the Israeli defense ministry declined to comment when the Financial Times reached out.
LeBlanc also previously claimed that two of the company’s Phantom MK-1 units went to Ukraine for testing in frontline reconnaissance and logistics roles in February 2026.

But Craig Smith , an independent journalist and host of the podcast Eye on AI , described tagging along during the delivery of the Phantom robots to Ukraine. He said that the robots never made it to Ukraine because they were stopped at the border with Poland.

When questioned by Smith, LeBlanc only said that Foundation had conducted a pilot demonstration at an undisclosed location, without clarifying whether the robots ever reached Ukraine. LeBlanc also walked back a claim that Foundation had demonstrated its humanoid robots to the Ukrainian government organization Brave1.

Promotional videos showing Foundation’s humanoids have not provided evidence that the robots are ready for battlefield deployments. For example, a “mortar demo” video on the company website dated to May 2026 shows a person handing a mortar shell to one of the humanoid robots, which slowly lowers the shell over the muzzle of a mortar weapon before finally dropping it in.

Whatever happens to Foundation, humanoid robots remain largely unproven technology and have yet to fulfill company promises that they can become general-purpose robots handling many different tasks. Companies have just begun testing and deploying such robots in greater numbers within relatively controlled environments such as factories and warehouses.

Similarly, humanoid robots have not yet had any impact on the battlefield. Instead, pioneers in robotics warfare such as the Ukrainian military have focused on developing and deploying unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs)—robotic vehicles that roll along on wheels or tank-style caterpillar tracks.

While defending against the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Ukrainian military has increasingly deployed more ground robots along with swarms of flying drones to make up for a shortfall in human soldiers compared to Russia. Such ground robots have typically been tasked with performing risky supply runs or evacuating wounded soldiers from frontline positions, but have also entered combat while wielding projectile weapons or even explosives when equipped as roving bombs.

Most recently, Ukraine has deployed armed ground robots directly into combat through both amphibious landings and through airdrops . In 2026, part of Ukraine’s counteroffensive success in rolling back Russian territorial gains has included dropping military robots from drones in airborne assaults behind Russian frontline positions.

items.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
paras: Dormant Defect Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365 A hidden bug, shifting traffic, and reduced capacity led to cascading failures.

Credit: Getty Images Credit: Getty Images Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav A hidden defect in Microsoft’s cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company’s history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft’s report lists the incident’s final status as “a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents.”

Microsoft’s preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14.

The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft’s cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft’s incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company’s status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report , and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft’s service-health updates .

Microsoft attributes the outage to three factors. A change deployed to Microsoft’s cloud gateway starting in July created a bug where, under certain conditions, CPU and memory resources could become exhausted and unresponsive. Microsoft contends that the defect was never discovered in pre-release testing because the hardware used was less powerful than some systems already deployed in production, where higher CPU core counts on newer machines apparently contributed to the lockout.

The second factor was server load. Microsoft said that “Traffic shifts during standard network maintenance and upgrades exposed a latent bug.” The company keeps two independent gateway systems in place to access Microsoft 365 for resilience. If one system encounters trouble and users can’t get through the front door, the other is opened to keep traffic flowing. According to the report, about 15 hours prior to the outage, traffic from Teams was shifted from the alternate gateway to the primary, where Exchange Online access is maintained. The switchover was a standard fail-safe, but it left the gateway handling more traffic, with a different mix of requests than before. As requests continued to pile up, affected servers exhausted their capacity and refused new connection requests.

The traffic shift exposed a third factor: infrastructure capacity. An existing fault meant that Microsoft’s gateway server fleet was operating at 14 percent below optimal conditions. That missing headroom could have normally absorbed the demand, but when combined with the changed traffic patterns and underlying defect, it left the gateways with lock contention as requests kept piling up.

As US business operations began hitting their daily peaks, the gateway servers began to freeze. Backup systems that shifted requests away from unresponsive servers did their job, but were met with the same lockouts on the supposedly healthy backup gateways. This created a snowball effect, leaving more than 80 percent of Microsoft’s affected gateway servers frozen in the sweep. Mechanisms in place to isolate affected systems by region seem to have failed. Microsoft’s current report doesn’t address why these isolation systems may have failed.

Recovery took longer than normal because the fix required a targeted system update from Microsoft engineers. Attempts to restart the gateway servers were ineffective; when the servers came back online, large request queues were still waiting for access, immediately triggering the same resource exhaustion that contributed to the outage in the first place. Microsoft says that services like Teams, OneDrive, and other Office applications could be routed away from the affected infrastructure, but scaling limitations stopped Exchange Online from making a similar move.

Since the bug from July was still undiscovered, system rollbacks were equally ineffective. Simply returning to a previous state where things were “working” couldn’t happen, because the ghost was already in the machine. Servers were patched and returned to service gradually, and Microsoft says it has added additional capacity and traffic-distribution guardrails to try to avoid anything similar happening again. Microsoft also extended delivery timeouts on affected emails to stop delayed messages from bouncing back as undeliverable.

Microsoft expects to publish its full final incident report on November 20. This final report may provide additional clarification on why the regional isolation systems failed and what corrective actions will be taken to ensure this type of outage can be avoided in the future. All of Microsoft’s cloud services appeared online and operational as of Monday morning.

items.title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
paras: Put the cloud on the map Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity Study attempts to tally hyperscalers’ energy use and emissions.

45 ... ... ... Credit: Cavan Images / Peter Essick Credit: Cavan Images / Peter Essick Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built.

A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. They weren’t able to differentiate between AI compute and more traditional data services, but it provides a clear point of reference to track moving forward.

The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts.

In a way, that makes this a very conservative estimate, since 272 facilities believed to be large data centers were left out. But if you’re interested in AI data centers, specifically, it’s also true that some of the facilities included may not fall in that category.

That fact also introduces some uncertainty in the actual power usage of these data centers. Relying on other research, they use a range—some conventional data centers run at an average of about 48 percent of capacity, while AI training loads have been running higher, at around 70 percent.

Putting that together, the total power usage for the year by these 403 data centers was estimated at 68 to 99 terawatt-hours. That amounts to 1.5 to 2.2 percent of total US electricity use, on par with the total used by Wisconsin or Indiana.

A recent Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report estimated the total electricity use of all data centers of any kind in the US (minus crypto mining) at 76 terawatt-hours in 2018. In 2024, that number was up to 192 terawatt-hours. That means the hyperscale data centers identified by this study account for something like one-third to one-half of all data center energy use.

The researchers also wanted to estimate the greenhouse gas emissions associated with generating all that electricity. It’s fairly straightforward to get a reasonable number here—calculate the mix of generation in each data center’s region of the grid, and apply that CO 2 per watt-hour rate to a data center’s electricity use.
This yields 21 to 31 million metric tons of CO 2 for the year. That’s around 0.5 percent of total US fossil fuel CO 2 emissions.

These data centers aren’t located in areas of especially clean energy—their energy mix was only slightly cleaner than the US average. About 54 percent of the electricity was generated by fossil fuel power plants (dominantly natural gas), with 25 percent from renewables, and 21 percent from nuclear.

This doesn’t include any “behind-the-meter” generation on-site, though. The xAI data center in Tennessee notably ran a fleet of natural gas turbines during this study’s time period, for example. Cleanview, which describes itself as a market intelligence company, has tracked a boom in on-site generation since early 2025, including 116 current or planned data centers. While this may not affect this study’s numbers much, it is becoming increasingly significant over time.

This matters because the types of generators being used are much less efficient than utility power plants, emitting 60 to 80 percent more greenhouse gases to produce the same amount of electricity. (Conversely, if a data center built solar generation instead, it could reduce the carbon footprint of its energy.)

Although this study can’t pinpoint the energy use of AI data centers alone, repeating this analysis in subsequent years could reveal the growth related to the AI buildout—at least as long as that buildout lasts.

items.title: November 17, 1991: The day Pete Sampras claimed his first season-ending ATP Masters Cup
paras: On this day in tennis history, one young American beat a compatriot to win his first ATP Masters Cup.
On this day, November 17, 1991, in Frankfurt, Pete Sampras beat Jim Courier in the final (3-6, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4) to claim his first title at the season-ending Masters Cup .

For the young American, who had lost his US Open crown two months earlier – to the same opponent – it was a relief to win such an important title after a hard season. It was also the first of five titles claimed by the future world No 1 at the year-end Masters Cup, which would be a record at the time (eventually broken by Roger Federer in 2011). Although he was an integral part of a golden American generation, along with Andre Agassi, Michael Chang and Courier, he was the last of them to become an elite player.
items.impact: Courier’s career took off in 1991: after clinching the titles at both Indian Wells and Miami, he triumphed at Roland-Garros to everyone’s surprise, beating his rival Agassi in the final (3-6, 6-4, 2-6, 6-1, 6-4).

items.title: How Maria Sharapova got on the year after winning the WTA Finals as Mirra Andreeva repeats feat
paras: What Mirra Andreeva has already accomplished at such a young age is astounding. At just 19 years of age, this year marked a standout for her, claiming her first Grand Slam title in Paris before capping the season off by winning the WTA Finals as well.

However, she is not the first teenage phenomenon to take the sport by storm, nor will she be the last. In fact, despite the hugely impressive nature of her WTA Finals triumph, she is still not the youngest to have ever won it.

That title belongs to Maria Sharapova , a player who Mirra Andreeva likely would not mind following in the footsteps of. Andreeva turned 19 this year, and is therefore just a year older than Sharapova was when she won the first and only WTA Finals title of her career.
items.impact: Sharapova began her 2005 campaign in Melbourne, enjoying an impressive run to the semi-finals.

items.title: Medvedev confirms he will keep Golubev as coach next year, “for the moment”
paras: Daniil Medvedev, who opened his ATP Finals in Turin with a straight-sets win over Flavio Cobolli, said his work with coach Andrey Golubev, started on a trial basis in Cincinnati in August, will go on in 2027, at least for now.
Daniil Medvedev plans to keep working with coach Andrey Golubev next season, but he left himself a small margin.

“It’s working well so far, so we definitely going to continue next year for the moment,” the Russian said in Turin after his 7-6(4), 6-3 win over Flavio Cobolli at the ATP Finals. Medvedev was speaking at his press conference on Monday night, after a match that lasted 1 hour and 27 minutes and in which he did not face a single break point. Asked about Golubev for next year, he gave a short, clear answer, with the “for the moment” attached.

items.title: “The best chance to beat him”: Medvedev sees an opening against Alcaraz in Turin
paras: After his opening win at the ATP Finals in Turin, the Russian explained why the fast indoor court could work in his favour on Wednesday against the Spaniard, who beat him in Vienna in October and has not lost indoors in 2026. Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
